note: Every render reads this file. scripts/disclosure_lint.py enforces it; nothing ships with a lint failure. Edit the terms to match your situation.

internal.description: The BragDoc itself (render.py bragdoc). Only you see it. Everything allowed: full project detail, security specifics, all contacts, internal figures.

resume.description: Every resume (render.py resume-extensive and any resume built from the BragDoc).
remove: anything in an entry's public_constraints (e.g. no security details tied to a named client)
allowed: engineering metrics (latency, throughput, test counts, coverage)
resume.contact_note: Resumes always use the personal email, even once email_domain exists.

public.description: A personal website (not included), including its downloadable resume (render.py public-resume).
remove: vulnerability class names (keep the achievement: 'hardened external document fetching', not the class name)
all employer money figures, absolute or relative
public.contact_note: The domain email is for the public channel only; never phone, never personal email.

public_constraints: Per entry: entries.jsonl -> public_constraints. Applies to the resume and public channels.
notes: Term lists are regexes. Acronyms and names are case-sensitive; phrases carry an inline (?i) flag.
always_banned: terms that may appear nowhere in data/ or any output (e.g. an employer you must not mention). validate.py enforces it.
current_employer_internal_names: internal identifiers of your current employer (codenames, flags, service names). Replace the placeholder.

names: each channel shows one form of profile.json names. A wrong casing of names.formal is an error everywhere; public blocks the formal form; a whole resume must contain it exactly. An all-caps design is CSS text-transform, never changed text.
